title: Bright Was the Guiding Star That Led
description: Bright Was the Guiding Star That Led in Tonic Solfa to ST. PETER, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 271 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Same”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. PETER; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Bright was the gui-ding star that led, With mild be-nig-nant ray, The Gen-tiles to the low-ly shed Where the Re-deem-er lay.

lines: Bright was the guiding star that led,
The Gentiles to the lowly shed
But lo! a brighter, clearer light
It shines through sin and sorrow's night
To guide us to our Lord.
O haste to follow where it leads;
Be rugged wilds, or flowery meads,
O gladly tread the narrow path
While light and grace are given;
We'll meekly follow Christ on earth,
And reign with him in heaven.

licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1853.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to ST. PETER by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
